guard: cotal history limit reads the four streams' limits with no limit flag and writes nothing, takes none for each age and count, sets INBOX and DLV with one pair, treats a limit set from none as lower and previews it per sender, agent lifecycle and DM pair under an operator census line, counts the stored copies a lower count removes before their durable delivered them, reports a refusal after an earlier stream changed as partial, and reports an update whose reply never came as an unknown outcome.
why: The suite drives the built binary, and its script builds it first, so each mutant is what the suite runs and
`afterRestore` rebuilds the restored source. The unknown cells run through a TCP hop that passes an update to
the broker and drops its reply, and the read-only cell has an observer on the open broker for STREAM.UPDATE.

mutations.name: H1 no limit flag is treated as a change
mutations.expectRed: with no limit flag, --json without --yes reads the four streams' limits
mutations.cell: with no limit flag, --json without --yes reads the four streams' limits

mutations.name: H2 the read-only call writes each stream back
mutations.replace:
if (readOnly) {
      for (const row of rows) await jsm.streams.update(row.stream, row.info.config);
mutations.expectRed: the read-only call publishes no STREAM.UPDATE
mutations.cell: the read-only call publishes no STREAM.UPDATE
mutations.note: An update of a stream with its own config changes nothing, so only the observer on the broker sees it.

mutations.name: H3 a refusal after a stream changed is reported as a refusal
mutations.expectRed: a later stream that moved is a partial change, exit 4, naming each stream's outcome
mutations.cell: a later stream that moved is a partial change, exit 4, naming each stream's outcome

mutations.name: H4 an update without a reply is reported as nothing changed
mutations.expectRed: a first update cut off before its reply is OPERATION_UNKNOWN, exit 3, not retried
mutations.cell: a first update cut off before its reply is OPERATION_UNKNOWN, exit 3, not retried
mutations.note: The broker applied that update, so "nothing was changed" would be false.

mutations.name: H5 the preview drops the operator census line
mutations.find: process.stderr.write("As the space's operator you see every agent and DM pair these streams hold entries for.\n");
mutations.expectRed: the preview says it is an operator census
mutations.cell: the preview says it is an operator census

mutations.name: H6 the stored-copy preview counts delivered copies as not delivered
mutations.expectRed: ...gives how many of each stored-copy lifecycle's removed copies were never delivered, or says it could not read them
mutations.cell: ...gives how many of each stored-copy lifecycle's removed copies were never delivered, or says it could not read them
mutations.note: The agent acknowledged its second copy and not its first, so a count of unacknowledged copies is not a newest run.

mutations.name: H7 none is not an age
mutations.expectRed: none for every flag leaves every stream with no age and no count
mutations.cell: none for every flag leaves every stream with no age and no count

mutations.name: H8 the inbox pair sets only INBOX
mutations.expectRed: the inbox pair sets INBOX and DLV together, and the DM pair sets DM
mutations.cell: the inbox pair sets INBOX and DLV together, and the DM pair sets DM

mutations.name: H9 an age from none is not a drop
mutations.expectRed: ...and each DM pair over the new count, with every DM older than the new age
mutations.cell: ...and each DM pair over the new count, with every DM older than the new age
mutations.note: An age set on a stream that had none deletes every entry older than it, unasked.

mutations.name: H10 a count from none is not a drop
mutations.expectRed: ...and each DM pair over the new count, with every DM older than the new age
mutations.cell: ...and each DM pair over the new count, with every DM older than the new age
mutations.note: A count set on a stream that had none deletes every entry past it, unasked.
